title: Preterite and imperfect: telling the story of Zapata and Villa

sections.content: You know the *indefinido* and the *imperfecto* from A2 Unit 22. The *indefinido* tells the events that happened and move the story on (*Zapata proclamó el Plan de Ayala*). The imperfect gives the background: who someone was, where they lived, what was going on (*Zapata era campesino*, *Villa vivía en el norte*). Use both to tell the story of the revolution in the north and the south.

items.spanish: Zapata era un campesino de Morelos.
items.english: Zapata was a peasant from Morelos.

items.spanish: En noviembre de 1911, Zapata proclamó el Plan de Ayala.
items.english: In November 1911 Zapata proclaimed the Plan of Ayala.

items.spanish: Villa vivía en el norte cuando formó la División del Norte.
items.english: Villa was living in the north when he formed the División del Norte.

items.spanish: En diciembre de 1914, Villa y Zapata se reunieron en Xochimilco.
items.english: In December 1914 Villa and Zapata met in Xochimilco.

sections.content: Ask yourself: is this a new event (preterite) or the situation around it (imperfect)? A date such as *en 1913* or *en noviembre de 1911* usually goes with the preterite; *era*, *vivía*, *querían* describe the background.
